stories.headline: IMD warns of possible cyclone formation in Bay of Bengal by Monday
stories.title: IMD warns of possible cyclone formation in Bay of Bengal by Monday
stories.summary: IMD warns of possible cyclone formation in Bay of Bengal by Monday
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: A weather system developing over the southeast Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by Monday evening and could further strengthen into a severe cyclonic storm, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast.
Amid the possibility of worsening weather conditions, fishermen have been advised to return to shore, with strong winds expected over the southwest Bay of Bengal until 18 November.
The Indian Coast Guard has also stepped up its preparedness, keeping ships and aircraft on standby to carry out rescue operations and safeguard lives and property.
According to the IMD, the low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal is expected to intensify on Sunday while moving west-northwestwards.
It is likely to develop into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the southeast Bay of Bengal by Monday evening.
The weather system could gain further strength after reaching cyclonic storm intensity, with the possibility of developing into a severe cyclonic storm.
However, the IMD has not yet specified any likely landfall location or timing.
The extent of the potential impact along the coast also remains unclear.
The immediate weather advisories include warnings of strong winds over the southwest Bay of Bengal and rainfall across parts of Tamil Nadu.
The IMD has forecast moderate rainfall on Sunday and Monday in districts adjoining the Western Ghats and southern parts of Tamil Nadu.
Chennai may also experience light rainfall on Sunday, according to the regional weather centre.
The strong wind warning over the southwest Bay of Bengal remains in effect until Wednesday, 18 November.

stories.headline: India should become developer, innovator and global leader in advanced tech: Rajnath
stories.title: India should become developer, innovator and global leader in advanced tech: Rajnath
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 15: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday called for making India not merely a user of advanced technologies, but also a developer, innovator and global leader in critical domains, as he emphasised the need to strengthen the country’s non-destructive testing ecosystem for better preparedness and self-reliance. He virtually addressed the 36th Annual Conference on Non-Destructive Evaluation & Enabling Technologies and the 15th International Symposium on Non-Destructive Testing in Aerospace. Singh stressed the importance of developing indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, promoting consistent quality assurance practices and ensuring the accuracy, reliability and integrity of testing results, particularly in strategic applications. He asserted that there can be no compromise on the integrity of testing results in strategic applications. "We must strengthen our indigenous capabilities in advanced inspection technologies, specialised sensors, evaluation equipment and associated software," the minister asserted. "Developing domestic capabilities in these areas is essential for reducing technological dependencies and securing critical defence supply chains. We must promote consistent quality assurance practices across the entire defence industrial ecosystem," he said. Public sector undertakings, private manufacturers, start-ups and MSMEs have an "important role to play" in this endeavour. "We must ensure that inspection results are accurate, reliable and traceable, and are based on robust procedures and appropriate standards followed by assessment by qualified professionals,” the defence minister said. The three-day conference, organised by the Indian Society for Non-Destructive Testing in Hyderabad, Telangana, has brought together over 2,000 professionals, researchers, industry experts and students to deliberate on the latest advancements, emerging technologies and applications in non-destructive testing (NDT), the defence ministry said. Singh stressed that the NDT technologies enable examination of the integrity of materials, components and structures without causing any damage to them. Elucidating the concept, he said that just as ultrasound and X-rays help examine the human body without surgical intervention, NDT techniques enable the detection of internal defects in critical components without dismantling or damaging them. Singh underlined that as Indian defence systems become increasingly sophisticated, every critical material, component, assembly and manufacturing process must meet the highest standards of quality and reliability. “Hidden defects can affect operational availability, increase maintenance requirements, reduce the service life of equipment and, in critical situations, jeopardise mission success. We need to move beyond a culture of merely identifying defects towards actively preventing them by embedding quality at every stage of the manufacturing process,” he said. Singh stressed that the progress of a nation depends not merely on the technologies it develops, but also on the quality, reliability and security of the systems it builds. In defence applications, including missiles, aircraft, naval platforms and spacecraft, quality is not merely a manufacturing requirement but an essential element of operational reliability and national security, he said. Emphasising the strategic significance of the sector, Singh said that for a country aspiring to achieve technological leadership, the importance of NDT cannot be overstated. He asserted that India's pursuit of “Aatmanirbharta (self-reliance)” in defence is not merely an economic objective but also a strategic necessity. Underscoring the importance of keeping pace with the rapidly changing global security environment, Singh said indigenous weapons, platforms and supporting systems "must deliver the highest levels of reliability and performance at all times". He urged professionals associated with the NDT sector to continuously upgrade their capabilities and keep the spirit of innovation alive in sync with emerging technologies and evolving security requirements. On the technological transformation underway in the field of non-destructive evaluation, he stressed that artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, advanced sensors, digital twins and predictive analytics are significantly expanding the possibilities of inspection and structural health monitoring. These technologies, he said, can improve the speed and consistency of inspections, facilitate the analysis of complex data and identify patterns that may not be easily detectable through conventional methods. Singh emphasised that the future lies in the intelligent integration of established inspection techniques with advanced digital technologies to make inspection processes more accurate, efficient and responsive to emerging industrial requirements. The minister called upon India to move beyond merely adopting these technologies and develop indigenous solutions tailored to its strategic and industrial requirements. Investment in research, advanced equipment, software and skilled manpower would strengthen domestic capabilities and enable Indian technologies to find markets internationally, he said.

stories.headline: ONGC takes charge of Cambay block as Vedanta records ₹379 crore impairment
stories.title: ONGC takes charge of Cambay block as Vedanta records ₹379 crore impairment
stories.summary: Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court on September 22, 2025.
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
event term: 'takes charge' in title weight 40
article_sentences: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) has taken over operations and control of the disputed Cambay offshore block from Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd following a Delhi High Court ruling, according to regulatory filings by the two companies.
Vedanta Oil & Gas Ltd has recognised an impairment charge of about Rs 379 crore against assets and receivables linked to the block.

The takeover of the CB-OS-02 block took effect on July 22, 2026, after the High Court's single-judge bench dismissed Vedanta's challenge to the government's decision not to extend the production-sharing contract, ONGC said in its quarterly filing.
The block was operated by Vedanta, which held a 40 per cent participating interest; ONGC held 50 per cent, and Invenire Petrodyne Ltd had the remaining 10 per cent.
The government, through a September 19, 2025, letter, declined to extend the contract and directed the operator to hand over the block to ONGC.
Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court on September 22, 2025.
The contract for the Cambay block expired on June 29, 2023.
Vedanta and its joint venture partners had applied for an extension on June 28, 2021, under the government's 2017 extension policy.
Vedanta's writ petition was dismissed on July 22, 2026, resulting in the vacation of an interim stay that had earlier directed that status quo be maintained.
ONGC subsequently took over the block and applied for a petroleum lease on July 28, 2026.
The legal dispute, however, remains unresolved.
Vedanta appealed against the single-judge order before a division bench of the Delhi High Court.
